expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: The 'canceled' arm has only `canceledAt` and `cancellation`; `trialEndDate` appears solely in the 'trialing' arm

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: IDs are bare strings: `id: string; customerId: string; planId: string`. The only 'branded' comment is on `RetryCount = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3`, which is not an ID type

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Only `handleSubscription` is provided, which formats a display string; no transition function, allowed-transition map, or other constraint on state changes

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "preventing access to `trialEndDate` on non-trialing subscriptions"; "Prevents 'voluntary cancellation due to payment failure' contradictions"; "Can't exceed 3 retries"

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: No optional (`?`) fields anywhere; the primary recommendation is the per-state discriminated union
